thread:
Jordan M: quick sync — i'm sketching a spike to decide where quota checks and per-route telemetry live. gateway or sidecar? trying to capture rollout UX concerns.

Priya K: my lean: gateway for hard limits (billing, global quotas), sidecar for local heuristics (soft-shaping, dynamic throttles). keeps single source for billing counters.

Ben T: gateway-first simplifies tenant accounting but adds latency on every request if we do a synchronous quota RPC. can we async-check + allow short grace?

Nina R: agree with Ben. pattern: gateway does fast path check (cache/allowlist), if miss forward to quota-service. sidecar can do local token-bucket for momentary bursts.

Jordan M: sounds hybrid. telemetry-wise, which surface emits the route/method labels? gateway sees raw path, sidecar sees decoded method for gRPC.

Priya K: we should normalize telemetry at the gateway to avoid duplication — add a canonical route label when we transcode. internal gRPC still emits method, but gateway can attach route_id for console.

Ben T: for browser SDKs we will accept JSON. plan: Envoy edge routes -> transcoder -> internal grpc. keep sampling rules per surface to control cardinality.

Nina R: rollout UX: console should show percent traffic, quota headroom, sample error rate, and a small diff of proto schema if method changes. rollout should block if quota headroom < threshold.

Jordan M: +1. also need a clear failure-mode: if quota-service is unreachable, fallback policy = degrade to throttled mode (e.g., 50% tokens) and emit a high-severity alert tied to runbook.

infra-bot: alert rule provisioned: name=quota-service-unreachable, severity=sev1, runbook=/runbooks/quota-fallback.md

Priya K: proto evolution note: prefer additive changes. for breaking renames create a new method and route that slowly drains traffic. Console should show active clients still calling old method.

Ben T: implementation sketch (pseudo):

```
# Edge / gateway pseudo-config
listeners:
  - name: public-http
    match: /v1/*
    handle: transcoder -> gateway-quota-check

routes:
  - id: r.infer.rpc
    backend: internal-grpc:443
    quota: remote:quota.svc
    telemetry: labels: [route_id, tenant_id, method_name]

sidecar:
  local_throttle:
    bucket: 200ms_burst
    fallback: soft_reject
```

Nina R: also recommend telemetry tags for deployment canary id so console can correlate rollout variants with errors/latency.

Jordan M: ops ask: how heavy will gateway be? proto to json transcoding CPU/memory? important for Dedicated SKU sizing.

Priya K: transcoding cost depends on message sizes; recommended: keep small reference proto shapes for SDKs + use binary gRPC internally for heavy payloads. include quota-check sampling to limit telemetry volume.

Ben T: next steps: PoC -> Envoy config + tiny quota svc + sidecar token-bucket. we'll exercise outage fallback and console panels for canary/quota headroom.

Nina R: i'll draft console panel widgets (canary %, quota headroom, top tenants) and a quick mock of schema-diff UI.

Jordan M: assigning: @Ben T spike owner, @Nina R console mock, @Priya K proto compatibility checklist. demo target = next Tue. thanks.

Ben T: will open branch and link here. ping if you want to pair on Envoy filters. :rocket:
